skill: Identify a distinct parallel line by isolating y in a given standard-form equation and matching slopes among complete line choices.
reasoning_steps: Rearrange Ax+By=C to By=-Ax+C and y=(-A/B)x+C/B.
Read slope -A/B and compare candidate x coefficients, ignoring intercept except to exclude the same line.
Select the unique distinct line with equal slope.
invariants: Nonzero y coefficient and exactly one parallel distinct candidate.
Radio selection of a complete line; no unknown-parameter task.
Worked solution shows rearrangement, division, and slope comparison.
permitted_variations: Both signs of A and B, small integer or rational resulting slope, cancellable common factors.
Target constant and all candidate intercepts may vary independently, preserving distinctness.
Which candidate qualifies, its position, slope rank and sign may vary. Correct option must not have uniquely recognizable formatting.
Moderate and hard may increase sign/division decisions within the same algebra; source has only easy labels, so higher bands require explicitly authored calibration.
source_refs: q-110094 and q-22574: incomplete banks show rational positive and negative slope identification; no missing imported fields will be changed.
Lesson tutorial 8902 / 2a7600a0-ce9a-5126-866d-bc3d1cf82b41: distinct parallel lines have equal slopes; examples y=2x+4 and y=2x-5.
